CHIEF COMPLAINT
Patient presents to discuss smoking cessation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient reports smoking history starting in high school with experimental use progressing to regular daily use. Currently smoking approximately 1.5 packs per day. Smokes first cigarette within an hour of waking. Patient is motivated to quit, with upcoming fatherhood as a primary motivator. Previously attempted to quit by going cold turkey and successfully abstained for almost a year but resumed smoking due to work-related stress from layoffs and increased job responsibilities. Patient has recently joined a gym and started meditation to help manage stress. Patient has considered nicotine patch based on friends' recommendations. Patient has set quit date for next Monday, which is his birthday.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes
History of gout
Systolic murmur (previously discussed, being monitored)

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol for gout management

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is 44 years old. Smokes 1.5 packs of cigarettes daily. No other tobacco products used. Recently joined a gym and started practicing meditation for stress management. Patient is about to become a father, with baby expected any day. Wife is pregnant. Quit smoking cold turkey for almost a year previously but relapsed due to work stress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Blood pressure 128/88, heart rate 68, respirations 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, 2/6 systolic murmur noted (known, being monitored).
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally, no expiratory wheezes, no rales or rhonchi.
Neck: No lymphadenopathy, no carotid bruits appreciated.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Patient counseled on benefits of smoking cessation, especially given history of gout and type 2 diabetes. Quit date set for next Monday. Starting 21 mg nicotine patch on quit date with plan to decrease dosage over time. Patient instructed to change patch location daily to avoid skin irritation. Follow-up appointment in two weeks to assess progress and reevaluate patch dosage. Patient given handouts regarding common smoking triggers. Advised to continue exercise routine and monitor stress levels, particularly regarding work stress and upcoming fatherhood. Encouraged to continue meditation and consider adding yoga.

2. Type 2 diabetes: Continue current management with diet and exercise. Hemoglobin A1c to be ordered for next blood draw; results to be discussed at follow-up visit in two weeks.

3. History of gout: Continue allopurinol. Patient counseled to continue monitoring foods that exacerbate uric acid levels.

Follow-up appointment scheduled for two weeks.
